messages:
kevin: New hire installed redwoodctl from the Snap store on Ubuntu and localtest refused to pick up their ~/.config/redwood/profile. It used a profile in /var/snap/redwood/common instead and login never completed.

kevin: Steps: `snap install redwoodctl --channel=stable`, create `~/.config/redwood/profile` with name 'dev-user', then `redwoodctl localtest start --profile=dev-user` -> started with 'snap-default'.

priya: can you paste `redwoodctl config resolved --verbose` and any auth logs?

kevin: resolved: `candidates: /var/snap/redwood/common/.config/redwood/profile (snap-default), /home/kevin/.config/redwood/profile (dev-user). requested_profile: dev-user. selected: snap-default`

kevin: auth trace: 
```
[auth] spawning xdg-open -> failed: permission denied
[auth] falling back to device-code flow
[auth] polling... 120s
[auth] error: unable to open browser due to snap confinement
```

oliver: Snap packages run confined by default. They often remap or isolate home and intercept xdg-open. Two separate problems here: 1) resolver is preferring snap-provided profile over explicit request (shouldn't), 2) snap confinement is breaking browser-based login.

priya: agreed. The resolver bug we've seen for apt appears in other package types: explicit profile requests must be resolved by name across all candidate locations before first-match short-circuit. We'll file a CLI bug.

packaging-snap: Snap team note: we intentionally place example config at `/var/snap/redwood/common/.config/redwood/profile` for demos, but snaps shouldn't override user config. We can change where examples live. Filed PKG-SNAP-21.

oliver: snap confinement also restricts xdg-open and network callbacks in some desktop environments. Workarounds: `snap connect redwoodctl:browser-support` (if we publish that plug) or run the snap in classic mode (`--classic`) or use the deb package. Also `redwoodctl login --device-code` works around browser issues but is clunkier for onboarding.

kevin: tried `redwoodctl login --device-code --profile=dev-user` and it timed out because server responded to the browser flow expected client_id from home profile, but snap-default client_id was used instead. So resolver precedence breaks auth as well.

priya: OK action items: 1) CLI: when requested_profile provided, scan all config locations and prefer exact-name matches before falling back (DEVEX-1409). Add unit tests for snaps and other packaging. 2) Packaging: stop shipping active demo profile under `/var/snap/redwood/common` or mark it as example-only under `/var/snap/redwood/common/examples` (PKG-SNAP-21). 3) Docs: add onboarding note for snap installs explaining classic mode or how to connect interfaces and the device-code fallback.

ci-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-1409 and PKG-SNAP-21; opened PR #1509 that adds resolver-name-priority tests.

packaging-snap: quick workaround shipped as snap revision: moved demo profile to `/var/snap/redwood/common/examples/demo-profile.yaml` and left `/var/snap/redwood/common/.config/redwood` empty. Will push stable after QA.

kevin: new-hire unblocked by `snap run --shell redwoodctl` then `ln -s ~/.config/redwood /var/snap/redwood/common/.config/redwood` (hacky) or by installing the .deb. Not ideal.

oliver: we'll prioritize the CLI fix; packaging change is also low-risk. Thanks for filing repro steps and logs — super helpful. :thumbsup:
